approved: Tax Laws Amendment (Norfolk Island CGT Exemption) Bill 2016

The speaker moved an amendment to support the bill while calling on the government to make capital gains tax fairer and more sustainable, citing that wage growth is at 2% (an 18-year low) while house prices rise 10% annually, and that home ownership for 25- to 34-year-olds fell from 60% in the early 1980s to 30% today. They criticised the government for ruling out changes to the capital gains tax discount and for defending negative gearing, noting that former Treasurer Joe Hockey and former Liberal Premier Jeff Kennett have supported restricting these concessions.

The speaker supported the Tax Laws Amendment (Norfolk Island CGT Exemption) Bill 2016, which provides a full capital gains tax exemption on assets held by Norfolk Island residents before 24 October 2015. The bill is part of broader governance and tax system changes to improve infrastructure, health services, and welfare access for Norfolk Islanders.

The speaker supported the Tax Laws Amendment (Norfolk Island CGT Exemption) Bill 2016, which grants capital gains tax-exempt status to assets held by Norfolk Island residents before 24 October 2015, as part of broader reforms following the Joint Standing Committee's report "Same country: different world—the future of Norfolk Island." The speaker thanked Minister for continuing the reforms and named the Norfolk Island Advisory Council members Duncan Evans, Eve Semple, Melissa Ward, PJ Wilson, and Wally Beadman for their transition work.

The Tax Laws Amendment (Norfolk Island CGT Exemption) Bill 2016 provides a full capital gains tax exemption on assets held by Norfolk Island residents before 24 October 2015, as part of a broader reform package integrating the island into mainland taxation, social security, Medicare, and other services from 1 July 2016. The exemption addresses concerns about retrospective taxation and historical lack of asset documentation.
